tutorial.dismantle.blocked: Huh? N-no, no! You can't dismantle that Block right now.
tutorial.intro.1: Hey! I'm your instructor again today. Remember me?
tutorial.intro.2: Our job is to protect the Core. If it gets destroyed, the whole system goes down.
tutorial.intro.3: I've prepared two Green Blocks and one Red Block this time. First, let's confirm your starting Blocks!
tutorial.first.red.connect: Now, try connecting the Red Block to the two Red Blocks already there.
tutorial.colorblind.question: Wait... is it hard to tell Red and Green apart? You need to pick the Red Block this time...
tutorial.colorblind.prompt: We're working on a Color Vision Support mode for players who have difficulty distinguishing colors. It's still in development, so for now, your setting will be saved, but it won't affect the game.
tutorial.first.red.wrong:
...That was a mistake, right? It's okay. You can dismantle a wrongly placed Block with right-click, but you won't be able to place it again, so be careful...
I'll make an exception this time and let you place it again. Try dismantling the Block you just placed.
tutorial.first.attack.success: Nice! Connect three Red Blocks, and they'll merge into an Attack Block like this!
tutorial.second.green.connect: Now, connect the two Green Blocks to the Green Block above them to make a Healing Block.
tutorial.second.healer.success: There we go! Ready to get started?
tutorial.second.healer.fail: Hmm... Okay. Saving a Special Block for later can be a good strategy too! Ready to get started?
tutorial.gameover: Oh no... That didn't go so well. Don't worry. We'll get it next time!
tutorial.clear.shockwave: If you can hold out until the Shockwave is fully charged, you can wipe out all the enemies at once.
tutorial.clear.killall: Nice! You took them all out. You can pick off enemies one by one like this, but if you hold out until the Core is charged, the Shockwave can wipe them all out at once.
tutorial.glitch.last:
You've done great so far! You're picking this up so quickly. You're really something!
And now, for the final step...

analytics.consent.title: Gameplay Data Collection
analytics.consent.message:
Would you like to share gameplay data to help us improve KEEP CORE SAFE?

Data collected: randomly generated installation and session IDs, session duration and count, game and SDK versions, operating system, platform, device and connection information, country code derived from your network IP address (GameAnalytics does not store the IP address itself), tutorial and prologue progress, wave starts and results, rerolls, selected rewards, block merges, a summary of the number of Blocks on the board, Core HP percentage, and game over or quit states.

This data is used to analyze gameplay flow, difficulty, failure points, and feature usage to improve the game. We do not collect advertising IDs, names, email addresses, chat messages, precise location data, payment information, exact board coordinates, or complete HP history.

Your data is processed by GameAnalytics on behalf of the developer and may be processed overseas. Data retention and deletion follow the developer's privacy notice and GameAnalytics' latest retention policy. Under the current policy, detailed events may no longer be available in the dashboard after 1–3 months depending on the event type, while some aggregated data may be available for up to 12 months.

Sharing is optional. Declining will not restrict your use of the game, and you can turn it off at any time in Settings. Turning it off will only stop future data transmission; data that has already been sent will not be automatically deleted. For more information or to request access to or deletion of your data, please contact the developer.
